paras: The attempted lynching of John Cowan was an interrupted hanging at the Post Percheron horse ranch near Cheyenne, Wyoming, reported in a dispatch dated June 27, 1888. Cowan, a cowboy accused by his fellow workmen of rifling a trunk, was tried and sentenced to hang by the ranch's cowboys and had a rope around his neck when the foreman intervened. Cowan survived and was ordered off the ranch.
Cowan worked as a cowboy at the Post Percheron horse ranch near Cheyenne, where, according to the dispatch, "thieving had been going on for some time."

According to the Cheyenne dispatch, Cowan's fellow workmen caught him "in the act of rifling a trunk" and held an "impromptu trial," at which he was "convicted" and sentenced to be hanged. He was taken out and a rope was placed about his neck, and he was about to be swung off when Foreman Le Compte arrived. After what the dispatch called "strenuous efforts," Cowan was released and ordered to leave the ranch.

A condensed version in an Oregon weekly placed the attempted hanging at a corral and said the foreman "allowed him to escape." In that account the "enraged cowboys" followed Cowan and "administered castigation," and he reached Cheyenne "half dead" and told his story.
The Oregon summary stated that "no arrests were made." No report of an inquiry or of charges against the cowboys or Cowan appears in the coverage.

On June 28 the Beatrice Daily Express in Nebraska and the Press and Daily Dakotaian in Yankton printed the Cheyenne dispatch word for word under the headline "A Thelef [Thief] Narrowly Escapes Hanging," which treated the accusation of theft as settled. The Lebanon Express of Oregon ran a rewritten version in its "Telegraphic" digest on July 6, alongside murders and accidents, placing it at "Cheyenne, Mont." and adding the beating and the absence of arrests. Neither version commented on the cowboys' conduct or mentioned anyone's race.
The accounts differ on the ending: the Cheyenne dispatch says Cowan was released and ordered off the ranch, while the Oregon summary says he escaped and was then pursued and beaten.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of John Cowan
bases: Fellow cowboys tried Cowan for theft on their own authority, sentenced him to hang and put a rope around his neck before the foreman intervened (A2, A4).

The cowboys acted under the pretext of justice through an 'impromptu trial' with no lawful authority, but Cowan was not killed; both versions have him escaping alive (A2, A4). It is an attempted lynching.
The Cheyenne wire dispatch (A2, reprinted A3) and a differently worded weekly summary (A4) agree on the core event, the interrupted hanging of Cowan for theft, though they differ on what followed.

accounts.label: Cheyenne wire dispatch
accounts.gist: Cowan was caught rifling a trunk, tried and sentenced by the cowboys, and had a rope on his neck when Foreman Le Compte appeared; after 'strenuous efforts' he was released and ordered off the ranch.

accounts.label: Weekly news summary
accounts.gist: The foreman let Cowan escape from the corral, but the 'enraged cowboys' followed and beat him; he reached Cheyenne 'half dead' and told his story, but no arrests were made.

framing.detail: Nebraska and Dakota dailies ran the Cheyenne dispatch verbatim under 'A Thelef Narrowly Escapes Hanging', taking the theft as fact.
An Oregon weekly put it in a 'Telegraphic' epitome, noting the beating and that 'no arrests were made'.

versions.value: Released after the foreman's 'strenuous efforts' and ordered to leave the ranch
Allowed to escape by the foreman, then pursued and beaten by the cowboys, reaching Cheyenne 'half dead'

conflicts.note: A2 is the dated Cheyenne dispatch; A4 is a later condensed summary that adds the beating. The two need not be incompatible, but only A4 reports the beating.
The dispatch dateline 'Cheyenne, Wyo.' is the better evidence; the summary's 'Mont.' appears to be an error.

record_check.dossier: No event date is given; the only dated report is a Cheyenne dispatch of June 27, 1888, so the event occurred on or shortly before June 27.
The June 26 linked article is a hotel advertisement unrelated to the event; the first report found is June 28.
Cowan's fellow cowboys at the Post Percheron ranch (unnamed).
Attempted hanging (rope on neck, not swung off) and ordered off the ranch; one summary adds a beating by the pursuing cowboys.
